idea-plugin.name: WLZN OSS Browser
idea-plugin.description:
Browse and manage Alibaba Cloud OSS and Amazon S3 without leaving IntelliJ IDEA. WLZN OSS Browser brings bucket navigation, file transfers and everyday object operations into an IDE tool window.

Features

  • Multiple named OSS and S3 connections, including temporary session credentials.
  • Automatic per-bucket region discovery when Endpoint is left blank; optional manual endpoints for private networks and compatible services.
  • A lazy-loading bucket and folder tree, clickable breadcrumbs, prefix search and paginated object listings.
  • Upload files or entire folders, drag files into the browser, and download multiple objects or folders.
  • Resumable multipart uploads and segmented downloads, with progress, pause, resume, retry and cancellation controls.
  • Preview images and UTF-8 text, edit small text objects, and copy object paths or create temporary signed download links.
  • Create folders, copy, move, rename and delete objects. Inspect metadata, manage supported object ACLs, request archive restoration and clean unfinished multipart uploads.
  • Native IDE menus and light/dark theme integration.

Getting started

  1. Open Settings → Tools → WLZN OSS Browser and add a connection.
  2. Choose Alibaba Cloud OSS or Amazon S3 and enter your credentials. Region and Endpoint can be left blank for automatic routing.
  3. Open the OSS Browser tool window, select the connection and click Connect. An optional bucket name lets you connect without listing every bucket in the account.

Credentials and operation scope

Credentials are stored using IntelliJ Platform PasswordSafe, rather than in project files or ordinary plugin settings. Cloud permissions, bucket policies and encryption requirements remain under your control. Transfers connect to the configured storage service using the official cloud SDKs.

Copy and move operations are limited to the same connection and region. Text and image preview is limited to 5 MiB. This plugin does not include IAM administration, bucket lifecycle editing, object version-history management or cross-cloud migration.
